data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A single evaluation cannot distinguish genuine reliability gain from mere compliance on its own; the distinction is fundamentally longitudinal and mechanistic, requiring comparison across items where the checklist is misaligned with the latent structure of the domain.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the single evaluation includes a held-out adversarial item subset where checklist-cues and outcome-cues diverge, it can in fact separate compliance from genuine reliability, contradicting the claim.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the domain is such that checklist and outcome structure are logically identical, the distinction is vacuous and a single evaluation suffices.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Mere compliance tracks the checklist; genuine reliability tracks the latent outcome structure.
